title: Meta/WhatsApp Cloud API ingress conformance fixtures
notice: This is the preimplementation CONFORMANCE SPECIFICATION expressed as data.
ADR-0030's 2026-08-17 amendment authorizes exactly this connector, and the
implementation is evaluated against these unchanged request bytes.
internally consistent and identities are computable from provider items.

signing_keys._notice: TEST KEYS. Generated for this corpus, never used by any deployment, and deliberately self-describing so a scanner that finds one knows it is inert. A real signing secret must never appear in this repository.

signature_header.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
signature_header.algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 over the exact request body bytes
signature_header.comparison: constant-time over the whole header value, including the 'sha256=' prefix

response.body_rule: the value of hub.challenge, echoed verbatim, with no JSON wrapper

handshake.comparison: constant-time on hub.verify_token; a mismatch and a missing token produce the identical refusal

eligibility._rule: The handshake is what PRECEDES activation, so it must be answerable before the binding is enabled. Requiring an enabled binding is circular: Meta will not deliver an event, and the Cloud API will not save the callback URL, until the GET is answered.
eligibility._owner: dotmac-integration. HANDSHAKE_INSTALLATION_STATES in dotmac_integration.ingress (PR #188, OPEN at the time of writing). These values track the module; the connector never decides its own eligibility.
eligibility._binding_grain_note: A handshake asks only about the INSTALLATION. A configured-but-disabled BINDING answers the challenge and refuses a delivery — module test `test_a_configured_but_disabled_binding_answers_a_handshake_and_refuses_a_delivery`.
eligibility._allowlist_not_negation: An allowlist, not `!= retired`, so a state added later is a deliberate decision rather than a silent admission.
eligibility._vocabulary_warning: Sub's `disabled` is NOT the Integrator's `disabled`, and porting the constant would invert this rule. Sub has no `validating` state, so its installations sit at `disabled` while an operator configures the callback — which is why `verify_whatsapp_webhook_challenge` admits {disabled, enabled}. The Integrator has `validating`, so the pre-activation position is `draft`/`validating` and `disabled` means an operator deliberately took a working integration DOWN. The PROPERTY is identical in both: the challenge is answerable before enablement. The state NAME is not.
eligibility._also_refuses_note: In Sub this is a state check inside the challenge handler. In the Integrator it is a mint-time gate (compatibility, manifest pin, ingress mode) rather than a handshake-time one, so an endpoint that should not serve never acquires an address to serve on.

message.note: The wamid is provider-assigned and stable across redelivery and across regrouping into a different batch.

status.note: One outbound message yields several status callbacks. The message id alone is NOT an event identity: sent, delivered and read would collapse into one row.

error.note: Meta assigns no identity to a change-level error. The identity is derived from the ITEM, never from the request body, so the same error redelivered inside a differently grouped batch still deduplicates.

forbidden.request_digest: sha256 of the raw request body
forbidden.reason: Sub uses `meta:{sha256(raw_body)}` as the single provider_event_id for a whole request. That is one identity per REQUEST, not per event: two batches that share a message are two identities, so the shared message is recorded twice, and twenty good events inherit the fate of the one bad entry beside them.

fixtures.description: One inbound text message with a contact profile name.
An image message: media is referenced by provider media id, never fetched during normalisation.
A location message. Float coordinates must survive normalisation unrounded.
A delivery status callback for an outbound message.
A failed status for a message this deployment never sent, with a provider error code and no value-level metadata.

The batch case: three entries carrying two messages, two statuses for one outbound message, one structurally bad message and one change-level error. wamid.meta-1 is deliberately the same message as fixture 01, regrouped into a different batch.

provenance.composed_because: Sub has no multi-entry, partly-malformed fixture. Its receiver silently drops what it cannot parse, so the case it fails on was never captured.

fixtures.description: An empty batch. Meta sends these. Zero observations is a valid, acknowledged outcome and not an error.

provenance.composed_because: Sub's literal is the compact b'{"entry":[]}'; the bytes here are the same document pretty-printed, and the recorded signature is over THESE bytes.

fixtures.description: A reaction — a message type the first connector will not interpret. It must still be observed, with a reason code; it must never be silently dropped.

provenance.composed_because: Sub has no fixture for this because it produces no output: `reaction` is outside the qualifying set, `_text_body` returns '', and `if not sender or not body: continue` drops the message with no record. The fixture exists to make the drop visible.

shared_events._rule: Two fixtures share an event identity. A connector keyed on the request digest cannot see that; a connector keyed on the provider's own ids must.

tamper_cases.note: Same JSON document, different bytes. This is why verification is over the bytes received and never over a re-serialised body.
